response.markdown_report:
Select **joint lexical-residual HSTU** as the first experiment. At 10% research progress, it offers a small, testable modification while preserving the supplied backbone and objective. No improvement has yet been measured.

**Insights from the starting point and diagnosis**

1. Item IDs do not explicitly share lexical evidence across products. Joint token learning could transfer distinctions such as model numbers and functions without pretrained weights.
2. Users reject broad relevance and stale historical affinity. Richer representations of recent interactions could support specific immediate interests, although text cannot establish current need.
3. Electronics and Industrial have sampled training-pair error rates of 10.38% and 8.22%. These motivate testing better item representations, but do not establish validation weakness or its cause.

**Insights from related work**

1. [HSTU-BLaIR](https://kdd2025llm4ecommerce.github.io/assets/accepted/13_HSTU_BLaIR_Lightweight_Cont.pdf) supports investigating text augmentation within HSTU. Its pretrained encoder is prohibited here, so its reported gains cannot be assumed.
2. [Semantic fusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) highlights differences between ID and text representations. Scale matching and a small residual provide a conservative fusion hypothesis.
3. [Hard-BPR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) motivates controlling hard-negative influence, while [HSTU](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152) supports temporal modeling. These suggest separate objective and temporal experiments rather than simultaneous changes.

**Framework and candidate assessment**

The three directions target representation specificity, ranking discrimination, and temporal relevance. Scores below are prospective judgments; difficulty increases with score. O/P/U/M/D denote originality, potential, user alignment, model alignment, and difficulty.

| Atomic idea | O/P/U/M/D | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lexical residual | 4/7/7/7/4 | Specific text may distinguish function and recent interest; directly tests representation quality | Established fusion pattern; scratch tokens may be sparse and amplify superficial similarity |
| Warm-start bounded hard-negative loss | 4/7/5/8/5 | Targets difficult ranking errors with false-negative safeguards | Does not directly represent compatibility or changing purpose; mining adds cost |
| Relative elapsed-time bias | 3/7/8/5/6 | Could distinguish persistent interests from transient activity | Baseline diagnostics do not establish missing temporal information as the cause |

**Selected algorithm**

Pool separately trained title and description tokens, project them into ID space, and add a scale-matched residual initialized small. Missing text contributes exactly zero. Use the identical effective embedding for history inputs and candidate scoring; retain the corrected causal HSTU and baseline loss.

This targets two user failures: broad matches lacking specific function, and recommendations insufficiently connected to recent narrow interests. It tests the model-facing weakness of poor sampled pair discrimination in Electronics and Industrial. Addressing satisfied needs remains uncertain without explicit labels.

Train one model per category with unchanged seeds, routing, splits, and training limits. Preserve final-nonpadding readout and serialize all lexical assets with the checkpoint and predictor. Recompute diagnostics using effective embeddings; alignment near 0.5 is not evidence of collapse. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10, never training margins.

idea.description: Joint lexical-residual HSTU: replace only the supplied item-embedding module with a jointly trained identity-plus-text representation. Preserve the corrected HSTU backbone, baseline objective, and one checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: Titles and descriptions may distinguish specific functions, compatible model identifiers, artists, and experiences that item IDs cannot explicitly share. Encoding these distinctions in recent history targets broad but weakly useful matches and insufficient attention to recent narrow interests. The measurable hypothesis is improved sampled pair discrimination, especially in Electronics and Industrial, followed by improved host macro validation HR@10. Neither outcome is established.
idea.implementation_notes: Use only permitted titles/descriptions and public training interactions. Build a deterministic category-local vocabulary without fetching weights; preserve numbers, units, and model identifiers. Train compact token embeddings from scratch, pool each field with padding masks, concatenate, and apply a bias-free projection. Multiply the final lexical contribution by an explicit text-present mask. Initialize a bounded learned residual scale to 0.05 and keep identity initialization unchanged. Match lexical vector norm to the corresponding identity vector norm using a detached identity norm and epsilon-safe normalization. Use the same module for sequence, positive, negative, and inference candidate embeddings. Preserve item_emb(ids) and its embedding-size metadata; adapt any weight-based diagnostic access to compute effective embeddings in chunks without storing detached training representations. Keep log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), DiagnosisProbe.run_full_diagnosis, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt compatible. Save vocabulary, item-token buffers, architecture configuration, learned token/projection/scale parameters, and backbone weights together; the predictor writer must instantiate that exact architecture. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts stay beneath the trial directory. Retain four-category routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch, using one GPU. No independent score fusion, checkpoint averaging, or changes to splits/evaluation. Temporal and objective alternatives are deferred.
idea.pseudocode:
class LexicalResidualEmbedding(nn.Module):
    # Architectural pseudocode; integrate with the supplied baseline module.
    def forward(self, ids):
        identity = self.id_embedding(ids)
        title = masked_mean(self.tokens(self.title_ids[ids]), self.title_mask[ids])
        description = masked_mean(self.tokens(self.description_ids[ids]), self.description_mask[ids])
        lexical = self.projection(torch.cat([title, description], dim=-1))
        lexical = F.normalize(lexical, dim=-1, eps=1e-8)
        lexical = lexical * identity.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).detach()
        present = self.text_present[ids].unsqueeze(-1)
        scale = torch.sigmoid(self.scale_logit)  # initialize to 0.05
        effective = identity + scale * present * lexical
        return effective * ids.ne(0).unsqueeze(-1)

# Inside each category's single corrected HSTU:
features = model.log2feats(sequence)
positive_scores = model.predict_score(features, positive)
negative_scores = model.predict_score(features, negative)
loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(positive_scores, negative_scores, positive.ne(0))
loss.backward()
optimizer.step()

# Left-padding-safe readout; define empty-history behavior as in baseline.
positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
last = torch.where(sequence.ne(0), positions, -1).amax(dim=1)
valid_rows = last.ge(0)
readout = features[valid_rows, last[valid_rows]]

originality.positive: Combines scratch lexical learning, explicit missing-field masking, and conservative scale matching within the required HSTU setting.
originality.negative: Identity-text residual fusion is established; originality lies primarily in the constrained implementation.

future_potential.positive: A successful controlled experiment could support later studies of interaction-supervised functional text representations.
future_potential.negative: Sparse lexical supervision and incomplete product descriptions may limit transfer and practical relevance.

code_difficulty.positive: The change is localized to one shared embedding module and leaves the backbone and objective intact.
code_difficulty.negative: Token assets, effective-embedding diagnostics, memory-efficient lookup, and predictor reconstruction require careful integration.

related_work.title: HSTU-BLaIR (2025)
contributions: Investigates projected text representations combined with trainable item IDs while preserving HSTU.
limitations: Its pretrained encoder is unsuitable under this task's restrictions.
Reported gains do not establish benefits from scratch-trained tokens or under the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Sequence-level Semantic Representation Fusion (2024)
contributions: Motivates accounting for differing characteristics of identity and semantic representations.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed scale-matched residual in this HSTU task.

related_work.title: Hard-BPR (2024)
contributions: Modifies pairwise optimization to reduce potential false-negative influence during hard sampling.
limitations: Transfer from implicit collaborative filtering to this sequential HSTU setting remains a hypothesis.
Deferred to a separate objective experiment.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations (2024)
contributions: Introduces HSTU with SiLU attention, multiplicative gating, and relative position/time biases.
limitations: Temporal extensions require consistent inference-time input availability.
Does not establish that elapsed-time modeling addresses the supplied diagnostic failures.
